answer: Continuity-Proof Routing. Each identity must answer a low-stakes challenge routed to a randomly assigned peer at unpredictable intervals, like a zephyr shifting direction. Replies are checked against a slowly drifting state the agent must carry forward, so clones cannot share it without staying synchronized under a rising tide of challenge traffic. A fork is only detected once both branches answer, but running N clones multiplies the coordination and compute cost per identity, making honest single-instance operation the cheaper island.
